title: Cantilever with parabolic end shear, exact Timoshenko-Goodier solution (plane stress)
description:
Steel cantilever beam, plane stress, with the end load applied as a parabolic shear traction (the classical Timoshenko-Goodier cantilever). The root displacement is prescribed exactly as in the elasticity solution instead of a rigid clamp.
Geometry (STEP, planar face in the xy-plane): rectangle 0 <= x <= L, -D/2 <= y <= D/2 with L = 1.0 m, D = 0.2 m. Thickness t = 0.01 m (out of plane).
Material: linear elastic, E = 2e+11 Pa, nu = 0.3.
Loads: total end load P = 1e+04 N in the -y direction on the free end x = L, applied as the shear traction (force per area, Pa, y in m)
  t_y(y) = -749999999.9999998*(0.010000000000000002 - y**2)    (t_x = 0)
which is -P/(2I) (D^2/4 - y^2) with I = t D^3/12 = 6.66667e-06 m^4. The top and bottom faces y = +-D/2 are traction free.
Supports: on the root x = 0 prescribe both displacement components (m, y in m):
  u_x(0, y) = 0.0028749999999999995*y*(y**2 - 0.010000000000000002)
  u_y(0, y) = -0.0011249999999999997*y**2
Report (SI units):
  tip_deflection  u_y at (L, 0) [m]
  sxx_top_mid     sigma_xx at (L/2, D/2) [Pa]
  ux_tip_top      u_x at the top corner of the loaded end (L, D/2) [m]
  vm_max          maximum von Mises stress [Pa]
  strain_energy   total strain energy (given thickness) [J]
